title: Tablet and Vial Visual Defect Detection
summary: Vision models that flag chipped, cracked, spotted or broken tablets and cap, crimp, glass or particle defects in vials, sending uncertain units to manual inspection and storing every reject image.

seo.title: Tablet and Vial Defect Detection with AI Vision | VipraTech
seo.description: AI vision for tablet and vial inspection: chips, cracks, spots, cap and crimp faults and visible particles, with reject images and inspector review.

designed_for: Production Manager, Solid Orals or Injectables

problem.intro: Tablets are inspected after compression and coating, and injectable vials and ampoules are inspected for particles and container defects before packing. Much of this is still done by trained inspectors at booths or sorting belts, followed by AQL sampling, and fatigue makes results vary across a shift.

pain_points.title: Fatigue and variability
pain_points.detail: Manual inspection depends on concentration, and detection of small chips or particles varies between inspectors and over long shifts.

pain_points.title: Fixed-threshold systems reject good units
pain_points.detail: Older automated inspection uses fixed rules that reject good units for embossing shadows or glass reflections and need constant retuning.

pain_points.title: Defect data goes unused
pain_points.detail: Reject counts are recorded, but images and defect types are rarely kept, so recurring tooling or coating problems surface late.

pain_points.title: Qualification effort
pain_points.detail: Every change to an inspection system needs defect libraries and requalification, which teams struggle to keep current.

solution.overview: We build defect detection models trained on images of your own products. For tablets, the model classifies chips, cracks, capping, black spots, embossing faults and coating defects on a sorting belt or inspection drum. For vials and ampoules, it checks cap and crimp, fill level, glass cracks and visible particles from images captured on your inspection machine or a dedicated camera station. Each unit gets a defect class and a confidence score. Clear rejects are removed, uncertain units go to a manual inspection lane, and every reject image is stored with its class for trending.
capabilities: Classifies tablet defects such as chips, cracks, capping, spots, embossing faults and coating defects
Inspects vials and ampoules for cap and crimp faults, fill level, glass cracks and visible particles
Sends low-confidence units to a manual inspection lane instead of forcing a decision
Builds a labelled defect library from your rejects for qualification and retraining
Trends defect types by batch, machine, punch set or filling line
Works with images from existing inspection machines where they can be exported

workflow.title: Build the defect library
workflow.detail: Inspectors label images of good units and known defects from your products to create training and challenge sets.

workflow.title: Train and challenge test
workflow.detail: The model is trained and tested against a fixed challenge set before it sees live production.

workflow.title: Capture and classify
workflow.detail: Cameras capture each tablet or container, and the model assigns a defect class and confidence score.

workflow.title: Route by confidence
workflow.detail: Clear passes continue, clear rejects are removed, and uncertain units go to the manual lane.

workflow.title: Inspector decision
workflow.detail: A trained inspector checks uncertain units, and the decision is added to the labelled library.

workflow.title: Trend and report
workflow.detail: Defect counts and images per batch go to production and QA for investigation and product quality review.

inputs: Images of good and defective units from your products
Defect catalogue with definitions and criticality
Line images from cameras or existing inspection machines
outputs: Pass, reject or uncertain decision per unit
Defect class and confidence with image
Trend reports by machine, tooling or filling line
human_in_the_loop: Trained inspectors decide every uncertain unit and confirm the labels used for retraining. QA approves each new model version after challenge testing, and AQL sampling continues as your batch-level check.
integrations: Inspection machines or sorting systems with image export
MES or ERP for batch and machine data
Data platform for product quality review trending
guardrails: Challenge sets with known critical defects run at start-up and after any change
Model updates only through change control with documented test results
Uncertain units always go to manual inspection
No retraining on labels an inspector has not reviewed
Critical defect classes tuned to avoid misses, accepting more manual checks
compliance_notes: Supports pharmacopoeial expectations for visible particles in injections, such as USP chapters 790 and 1790 and Ph. Eur. 2.9.20, alongside your AQL programme.
Models and inspection recipes are validated as part of a GMP computerised system, with versioning and audit trails aligned to EU GMP Annex 11 and 21 CFR Part 11.

pilot.scope: One tablet product on a sorting belt, or one vial size on an existing inspection machine, using offline images first and then a shadow run alongside manual inspection.
deliverables: Labelled defect library for the pilot product
Trained model with challenge test results

faqs.q: How many defect images do we need?
faqs.a: It depends on the defect type and how rare it is. We start with your existing reject samples and images, and create seeded defects where real examples are scarce. The pilot report states how many examples each class had.
It changes their work rather than removing it. Inspectors handle uncertain units, label new defect types and run challenge tests, and AQL sampling continues.

faqs.q: Can it work with our existing inspection machine?
faqs.a: Often, if the machine can export images. Otherwise we specify a separate camera station. We confirm this in the first week of the pilot.
Against a fixed challenge set of known defects, documented in a test report and re-run after any model or hardware change. We provide the documents your validation team needs to qualify it.
